source_text:
6.11 Αἰσχυνθείησαν καὶ
ταραχθείησαν σφόδρα πάντες οἱ ἐχθροί μου. ∆αιμόνων τὸ διὰ παντὸς τὴν ἀνομίαν
ἐργάζεσθαι, ἀνθρώπων τὸ μὴ διὰ παντὸς, ἀγγέλων τὸ μηδὲ διὰ παντὸς, μήτε μὴ διὰ
παντὸς, ο περ ἐστὶν οὐδέποτε. – ̓Απὸ μοχ θηρῶν διαβουλιῶν ἀποπεσεῖν, οὐ κακὸν τῷ
ἀποπίπτοντι, οὐκ ἐρχομένῳ ἐπὶ τὸ μοχθη ρὸν αὐτῶν τέλος, ὡς οὐ καλὸν τῶν κρειτ
τόνων μὴ ἐπὶ τέλος ἐλθεῖν.
pass_a_gloss: Let-them-be-ashamed and let-them-be-troubled greatly all the enemies of-me. Of-demons the through all the lawlessness to-work, of-men the not through all, of-angels the neither through all, nor not through all, which is never. From wicked counsels to-fall, not evil to-the one-falling, not coming upon the wicked of-them end, as not good of-the better-things not upon end to-come.
pass_b_english: “Let all my enemies be ashamed and greatly troubled” (Psalm 6:11).
It belongs to demons to work lawlessness always, to men not always, to angels neither always nor not-always, which is never.
To fall from wicked counsels is not an evil for the one falling, who is not coming to their wicked end; as it is not good not to come to the end of the better things.

choices.term: μηδὲ διὰ παντὸς, μήτε μὴ διὰ παντὸς, ὅπερ ἐστὶν οὐδέποτε
choices.english: neither always nor not-always, which is never
choices.why: Angels are not in the ‘always’ of demons nor the ‘not always’ of men; Origen glosses that pair as never.

choices.term: Ἀπὸ μοχθηρῶν διαβουλιῶν ἀποπεσεῖν, οὐ κακὸν
choices.english: to fall from wicked counsels is not an evil
choices.why: Same ἀποπίπτω as 5.11: falling from bad counsel is a good miss. Not ‘falling is always evil’.
rejected: falling from wicked counsels is an evil
they must finish the wicked end
